headline: BNP nominates Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir for presidential election
summary: The party submitted his nomination papers to the Election Commission today after he resigned from his posts as Secretary General and Standing Committee member.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has submitted the nomination form of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to the Election Commission (EC) for the 23rd presidential election.
A BNP delegation delivered the papers to Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, the returning officer, at the CEC's office in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The nomination was proposed by BNP Standing Committee member Moyeen Khan and seconded by Gayeshwar Chandra Roy.
Earlier today, BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman announced Mirza Fakhrul as the party's presidential candidate during a high-level meeting at the Cabinet Division conference room.
Following the nomination, Mirza Fakhrul resigned from his roles as the party's Secretary General and member of its Standing Committee.
Mirza Fakhrul currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Thakurgaon-2 constituency and has been the LGRD minister since February 17 of this year.
caption:
BNP has officially entered the race for the 23rd presidential election by nominating Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has submitted the nomination form of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to the Election Commission (EC) for the 23rd presidential election.

A BNP delegation delivered the papers to Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, the returning officer, at the CEC's office in Agargaon, Dhaka.

The nomination was proposed by BNP Standing Committee member Moyeen Khan and seconded by Gayeshwar Chandra Roy.

Earlier today, BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman announced Mirza Fakhrul as the party's presidential candidate during a high-level meeting at the Cabinet Division conference room.

Following the nomination, Mirza Fakhrul resigned from his roles as the party's Secretary General and member of its Standing Committee.

Mirza Fakhrul currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Thakurgaon-2 constituency and has been the LGRD minister since February 17 of this year.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets as [[Bangladesh bowl out Australia for 198]]
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets as Bangladesh bowl out Australia for 198
summary: The Tigers are in the driving seat on Day 1 of the first Test in Darwin, ending the day at 96/1 after a historic bowling display.
details: Bangladesh enjoyed a dominant opening day at the Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out a full-strength Australian side for 198 runs.
Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, claiming 6 for 55 and becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul in Australia.
Steve Smith was the only Australian batter to pose a significant threat, scoring 71 runs despite early scares from the Bangladesh pacers.
Smith later admitted in a press conference that he had nicked a ball from Ebadot Hossain but was saved by the Real Time Snicko technology.
The Tigers ended the first day comfortably in control at 96 for one, trailing by just 102 runs with nine wickets remaining.
Bangladesh's fast-bowling unit showed remarkable consistency and precision, putting the hosts under pressure throughout the first innings.
caption:
A historic day for the Tigers! Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul destroys Australia for 198.

Bangladesh enjoyed a dominant opening day at the Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out a full-strength Australian side for 198 runs.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, claiming 6 for 55 and becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul in Australia.

Steve Smith was the only Australian batter to pose a significant threat, scoring 71 runs despite early scares from the Bangladesh pacers.

Smith later admitted in a press conference that he had nicked a ball from Ebadot Hossain but was saved by the Real Time Snicko technology.

The Tigers ended the first day comfortably in control at 96 for one, trailing by just 102 runs with nine wickets remaining.

Bangladesh's fast-bowling unit showed remarkable consistency and precision, putting the hosts under pressure throughout the first innings.
